content.title: THE {{ORGANS}} YOUR GROCERY LIST IS SECRETLY TAKING CARE OF
facts: **Pancreas** - Spinach, Pumpkin seeds, Broccoli - sulforaphane in broccoli helps calm inflammation around insulin-producing cells.
**Kidneys** - Red bell peppers, Cabbage, Onions - low-potassium and low-sodium, so they filter through without straining the kidneys.
**Bladder** - Cranberries, Watermelon, Celery - these keep fluid moving through the urinary tract instead of letting it sit stagnant.
**Gallbladder** - Beets, Olive oil, Lemon - a little healthy fat triggers bile flow instead of letting it thicken and stagnate.
**Spleen** - Pomegranate, Beef liver, Lentils - iron-rich foods restock what the spleen filters out of aging blood cells daily.
**Thymus** - Oysters, Shiitake mushrooms, Sunflower seeds - zinc here keeps this gland pumping out immune cells as you age.
**Joints/cartilage** - Bone broth, Sardines, Walnuts - collagen-building nutrients cushion the spaces between your bones.
**Follow along** - for more daily health tips like this.

caption:
Your pancreas works harder than most people realize, and broccoli actually helps it out - the sulforaphane it contains calms inflammation around the cells that produce insulin, so blood sugar swings hit a little softer. Your kidneys quietly filter your entire blood supply dozens of times a day, and cabbage makes that job easier because it's naturally low in potassium and sodium, meaning less strain pushing through the filtering units. And your gallbladder needs a nudge to actually release bile instead of letting it sit and thicken - a little olive oil at a meal is enough to trigger that flow. Of course, everyone's body is different, so listen to yours and adjust from there.
